title: Control-failure cards show the actionable structured cause and operation/correlation, not only a generic control_unavailable label
outcome: When a turn's host or control operation fails or is held (for example turn_begin control_unavailable, a begin-unknown hold, an admission refusal), the session's UI card shows the structured refusal or error cause the host already knows (the reason code and raw reason, the boundary or phase, whether the remote application started), plus the operation and correlation identifiers where available (operation name, prompt or message id, grant or attempt id), so the user and agents can act on it. A generic label appears only when no structured cause exists.
acceptance: The holder's note lists the control-failure and held card kinds, and for each the structured cause fields the host already records (including the SEV0 causalFailure fields from w-48618ba39f11) and whether the card renders them today.

A test shows a control-failure card (for example the begin-unknown hold whose raw reason is "named-root acknowledgement belongs to a superseded authority image") rendering its reason code, raw reason, boundary and correlation ids, and a card without a structured cause still rendering a clear generic message.
The fields are bounded and escaped for display (no unbounded raw dumps), and the session list and pane show consistent text.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact committed tree.
